text:
Lande c. Feldman

2020 QCCS 3782

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTRÉAL

No:

500-17-110921-197

DATE:

November 19, 2020

______________________________________________________________________

IN THE PRESENCE OF

THE HONOURABLE

LOUIS LACOURSIÈRE, J.S.C.

______________________________________________________________________

Irwin Lande

-and-

Claude-Andrée
Pion

Plaintiffs

v.

Glenn J. Feldman

Defendant

______________________________________________________________________

RECTIFIED JUDGMENT

______________________________________________________________________

[
1
]

Irwin Lande
(Lande) and Claude-Andrée Pion (Pion) ask for the issuance of a provisional
injunction ordering Glenn J. Feldman (Feldman) to cease communicating any
information pertaining to their private lives, to cease utilizing third party
entities, including the media, to disseminate defamatory statements and to
cease contacting relatives, business associates or contacts of theirs to obtain
details on their private life and their sources of income or assets.

[
2
]

Lande and Pion sued Feldman in December of 2019
alleging,
inter alia
, defamatory behaviour on his part. They now feel
that there has been a
crescendo
in Feldman’s conduct which warrants an
emergency order.

[
3
]

It is useful first to provide some background
and to summarize the proceedings already in the record. Many of the allegations
they contain are invoked in support of the demand for a provisional injunction
and have a bearing on the existence of the urgency necessary to seek extraordinary
redress from the Court.

* * *

[
4
]

The relevant facts, as appears from the
proceedings and exhibits available to the Court, are the following.

[
5
]

Lande is a businessman involved in real estate.
Pion has been his wife for some 21 years. They have four children.

[
6
]

Feldman is a lawyer and businessman in the real
estate field.

[
7
]

Feldman and Lande have known each other since
their teenage years, have been friends and, through the years, built a
significant real estate portfolio.

[
8
]

Lande’s parents, Martin and Mia Lande, are
Holocaust survivors who immigrated to Canada in the early fifties.

[
9
]

In 1983, Ludwig Delphiner (Delphiner), Martin
Lande’s relative, died. He left his property valued, according to Lande, at
approximately 900 000 $, to Martin Lande. Lande himself never
received any inheritance or benefits from Delphiner nor was he involved in Dephiner’s
estate or will. Delphiner’s life will be alluded to by Feldman in circumstances
hereinafter referred to.

[
10
]

Lande’s mother died in 2015, leaving him and his
immediate family a significant inheritance.

[
11
]

Lande claims that Feldman has changed since this
last event. He became aggressive towards him through harassment, death threats,
intimidation, extortion attempts, violation of privacy and defamatory
statements.

[
12
]

Lande filed complaints with the police at the
end of December 2019 and Feldman was arrested and charged for criminal
harassment and uttering threats to cause bodily harm. In February of 2020, the
charges were processed under the “Non-judicial treatment of certain criminal
offences committed by adults” program
[1]
.

[
13
]

Feldman’s behaviour led Lande and Pion to initiate
proceedings (the Application) in December of 2019 seeking 14.5 $ million
in general damages, 3 $ million in punitive damages and seeking that
Feldman refrain from violating their fundamental rights, notably the safeguard
of their dignity, honour and reputation and their right to the respect of their
private life.

[
14
]

In the Application, the Plaintiffs alleged,
notably, that in September and October 2019, Feldman contacted their entourage
to convince them that Lande is a crook who had stolen gold bars valued at
millions of dollars and that he was hiding in his house more than 180 $
million in illegally obtained gold bars which originated from the Nazis.

[
15
]

The Application also referred, notably, to the
death threats and to public disturbances caused by Feldman, including
disturbing the wedding of the daughter of a mutual friend in November of 2019,
at which he had been “disinvited”, where he had a truck parked in front of the
Windsor building, where the reception was held, displaying an illuminated
advertisement which read “No Feldman, No wedding”.

[
16
]

On or about October 9, 2020, Lande and Pion
amended their originating application (the Amended Application) to allege new
wrongful conduct on the part of Feldman, including his alleging that Lande is
in possession of 2.6 $ billion worth of gold bars inherited from Delphiner. The
latter was, according to Feldman, an officer in Hitler’s army who had
confiscated the gold bars and other possessions from Jewish war prisoners’
camps during the Second World War.

[
17
]

The Amended Application also alleges Feldman’s
continued harassment such as stalking. It refers to a 21 page Long-Form
affidavit (the Affidavit) dated March 31, 2020 sent to Justice Marie-Anne
Paquette after a judgment she rendered on parallel proceedings before the Commercial
Division of the Superior Court, with copies to Plaintiffs’ lawyers and third
parties, containing expressions of hatred and stating that it is Feldman’s duty
that the Plaintiffs not continue living on forbidden fruit, i.e. Nazi gold.

[
18
]

The Amended Application also refers,
inter
alia
, to the fact that, on June 24, 2020 Lande’s and Pion’s house was
smeared with a hideous graffiti
[2]
,
that on September 4, a journalist from the
Journal de Montréal
contacted
Pion’s nephew to ask him to supply information on his aunt and uncle and that,
on September 21, Feldman’s daughter published an ad on her Facebook page
looking for a video editor with experience with documentary film, which led
Lande to believe that Feldman was preparing a video to spread his hatred.

[
19
]

Finally, the Amended Application refers to the
fact that the same journalist from the
Journal de Montréal
showed up on
October 7, unannounced, at the house of prominent friends of the Plaintiffs to
talk about him, the request for comments having been declined.

[
20
]

The Amended Application also refers to Feldman
admitting having taunted Lande with messages to get him to admit his crime,
having disseminated libellous videos
[3]

where he recounts his “findings” on Lande’s role in the alleged stealing of
Holocaust victims’ property and where he states his “mission” to recover this
money. It refers to Feldman having stalked the Plaintiffs’ children, having
accused Lande of forging Delphiner’s will and having communicated with people
close to Lande and with organizations of the Jewish community such as B’nai
Brith and the Simon Wiesenthal Center for Holocaust victims to obtain
information about the Plaintiffs.

[
21
]

The Court will now address the demand of which
it is seized.

* * *

[
22
]

The proceeding now before the Court is a Motion
for provisional and interlocutory injunction dated November 10, 2020.

[
23
]

The Motion refers, essentially, to the facts
already alleged in the Application and Amended Application:

a)

Feldman claims that Lande’s wealth consists of
gold bars stolen from Holocaust victims passed down from Delphiner;

b)

Feldman has been spreading this information
about Lande’s wealth to Lande’s and Pion’s friends and relatives;

c)

The institution of the proceedings in December
of 2019 did not bring an end to Feldman’s spreading hatred and falsehoods;

d)

The Affidavit defamed and slandered the
Plaintiffs;

e)

In late May or June, 2020, Feldman was arrested
on charges of extortion, intimidation, harassment towards Lande, mischief and
threat to cause death or bodily harm and he was released on June 26 under
conditions such as not to contact Lande or be within 300 meters of his
residence or his place of work
[4]
;

f)

In early October 2020, Feldman visited, with a
journalist from the
Journal de Montréal
, unannounced, at the residence
of prominent family friends of Lande and Pion to seek comments from them on Lande;
and

g)

The
Journal de Montréal
published, on
October 31, 2020, an article entitled “L’or nazi autour d’une querelle
judiciaire” (the Article)
[5]
.

[
24
]

The Article states,
inter alia
:

Le développeur d’une des maisons les plus
chères au Québec poursuit son partenaire d’affaires en diffamation, après que
celui-ci eut allégué qu’il aurait dissimulé dans sa résidence plus de 180 M$ en
lingots d’or qui proviendraient des nazis.

Glenn Feldman, un avocat et propriétaire
d’immeubles commerciaux, colporterait que son partenaire d’affaires de longue
date, Irwin Lande, aurait fait construire ce qui est actuellement une des
maisons les plus chères à vendre au Québec avec de l’argent volé d’un héritage.

(…)

Ces allégations étonnantes sont contenues
dans une poursuite déposée par Irwin Lande et son épouse contre Glenn Feldman à
la fin 2019. Les deux anciens partenaires et amis sont aujourd’hui à couteaux
tirés. Ils sont engagés dans plusieurs litiges de nature personnelle et
commerciale.

(…)

Selon les prétentions de Feldman rapportées
dans une autre poursuite (voir texte plus bas), Irwin Lande aurait bâti sa
fortune en bénéficiant de l’héritage d’un chimiste d’origine autrichienne qui
aurait travaillé à Montréal pour la firme Laboratoires Abbott. Il serait mort
en 1983.

Ce chimiste, Ludwig Delphiner, aurait
collaboré avec les nazis pendant la Deuxième Guerre mondiale, selon Feldman.

Des lingots d’or illégalement obtenus
provenant des nazis seraient cachés encore aujourd’hui dans la maison d’Irwin
Lande actuellement à vendre, toujours selon les prétentions de l’avocat
Feldman.

(…)

Irwin Lande et son épouse
mentionnent dans leur procédure que les parents d’Irwin sont eux-mêmes des
survivants de l’Holocauste. Selon le couple, les allégations de Feldman sont
fausses et hautement dommageables. « Il a violé la dignité, l’honneur et la
réputation des plaignants en produisant et en disséminant des informations
fausses, diffamatoires et vexatoires », plaident-ils.

« Alléguer auprès de l’entourage des plaignants
dans la communauté juive que les plaignants ont volé de l’argent des victimes
de l’Holocauste est une des pires insultes qu’on puisse imaginer », disent-ils.

[
25
]

The Article also refers to another lawsuit
instituted by Lande’s nephews:

Chimiste exemplaire ou nazi?

Ludwig Delphiner, le chimiste au centre d’une
importante dispute entre deux anciens partenaires d’affaires montréalais,
a-t-il été un personnage exemplaire, reconnu dans son milieu, ou au contraire
un sinistre officier d’Adolf Hitler dans le Troisième Reich ?

Deux neveux d’Irwin Lande allèguent dans une autre
poursuite que Ludwig Delphiner est un cousin de la sœur d’Irwin Lande qui n’a
absolument rien à se reprocher. (Dans leur poursuite, Irwin Lande et son épouse
présentent de leur côté le chimiste Delphiner comme un cousin du père d’Irwin
Lande.)

Soldat décoré

« Il a mené par l’exemple durant toute sa vie en tant
que soldat décoré dans la Cavalerie autrichienne durant la Première Guerre
mondiale, chimiste en chef (à partir de 1930) chez Laboratoires Abbott et
membre de son conseil d’administration depuis 1947, de même que fellow de
l’Institut de chimie du Canada », allèguent Jonathan Jacob Feifer et Andrew
Feifer dans ces recours.

(…)

[
26
]

The Article contains images of Lande’s and Pion’s
house, their address and an image of Lande, the use of which he never
authorized.

[
27
]

The Article appeared on tvanouvelles.ca
[6]
and was translated on thecanadian.news
website
[7]
.
One of its authors was interviewed on QUB Radio streaming service.

[
28
]

A demand letter
[8]

was sent on November 3, 2020 to the
Journal de Montréal
, the authors of
the Article, TVA Nouvelles, QUB Radio and Québecor Media inc, notably to
emphasize that Lande was never asked for his comments and to ask for a
“retractation” of the Article. There was no follow-up to this letter.

[
29
]

Are the conditions met for the issuance of a
provisional injunction?

* * *

[
30
]

The criteria to issue an interlocutory
injunction are:

a)         an appearance of right;

b)         a serious or irreparable prejudice;

c)         the balance of inconvenience
[9]
.

[
31
]

In a recent judgement
[10]
rendered on an Application
for Leave to Appeal, Justice Robert Mainville of the Court of Appeal provided
an enlightening summary of the rules applicable to interlocutory injunctions:

[13]      Il est de jurisprudence constante
que les trois critères reconnus de longue date pour émettre une injonction
interlocutoire doivent être tous satisfaits, sauf circonstances
exceptionnelles. Dans les arrêts Manitoba (Procureur général) c. Métropolitan
Strores Ltd, ensuite RJR – MacDonald Inc. c. Canada (Procureur général), et
plus récemment Google Inc. c. Equustek Solutions Inc. et R. c. Société
Radio-Canada, la Cour suprême du Canada a affirmé que les demandes d’injonction
interlocutoires devraient normalement satisfaire chacun des trois volets du
test qui tire son origine de la décision de la Chambre des Lords dans American
Cyanamide Co. c. Ethicon Ltd. C’est aussi le cas au Québec.

[14]      Si certains tribunaux du Québec
ont affirmé à l’occasion que ce n’est que lorsqu’un droit est « douteux » – par
opposition à « clair » – que le juge saisi d’une demande d’injonction
interlocutoire doit procéder à l’évaluation comparative des inconvénients,
cette approche a été nuancée par la Cour dans l’arrêt Groupe CRH Canada inc c.
Beauregard dans des motifs qui ont été depuis repris par la Cour. C’est donc
dans le cadre de l’évaluation de la balance des inconvénients que le poids des
droits respectifs des parties peut être pris en compte, comme le laissait
entendre le juge Baudouin dès 1991 dans Gagné c. Bouliane : « […] la seule
contravention à une loi d’ordre public, sans que le degré de contravention en
soit déterminé, n’élimine pas obligatoirement la possibilité pour le juge
d’évaluer comparativement les inconvénients ».

[15]      Ainsi, sauf certaines rares
exceptions, même lorsque le requérant réussit à établir une forte apparence de
droit – comme cela doit d’ailleurs être le cas lorsqu’il s’agit d’une demande
d’injonction dite « mandatoire » – et un préjudice sérieux, le juge saisi de
l’affaire devrait généralement procéder à l’évaluation comparative des
inconvénients et ne devrait émettre l’injonction interlocutoire que si celui
qui la requiert satisfait également ce dernier critère.

[16]      Cela ne signifie pas que
l’apparence forte de droit ne joue aucun rôle dans l’analyse de la
prépondérance des inconvénients, bien au contraire. Ainsi, lorsqu’une apparence
forte de droit est établie, celle-ci peut faire pencher la prépondérance des
inconvénients dans le cadre de la pondération requise selon ce critère.

(References omitted)

[
32
]

In the case of an injunction asked on a
provisional basis, there has to be an urgency to remedy the situation
[11]
.

[
33
]

The Court will first deal with the matter of the
urgency.

[
34
]

Is this matter urgent?

[
35
]

It is obvious that the Article is, for the Plaintiffs,
the proverbial straw that broke the camel’s back. They argue that it is clear
that Feldman is the source of the Article and that his action is a prelude to further
actions on his part that will damage their reputation amongst their friends,
relatives, community and the public at large. This, in their view, creates a
situation of urgency.

[
36
]

In her book
L’injonction
[12]
, Me
Celine Gervais writes, on the notion of urgency:

La question de l'urgence mérite certes une
considération spéciale, puisque sans elle l'injonction ne saurait être émise.
En qualifiant l'urgence, on a déjà jugé qu'elle devait être «immédiate et
apparente». C'est le jugement Société minière Louvem inc. (
1990 CanLII 3829 (QC CS)
,
J.E. 90-384
(C.S.)
)
qui a le mieux défini le caractère de l'urgence. On y indique que dans la
mesure où les règles qui s'appliquent à l'injonction provisoire doivent
s'interpréter avec beaucoup plus de rigueur, seuls les cas extrêmement urgents
devraient être considérés pour son octroi. De tels cas peuvent survenir lorsque
même le délai pour obtenir une injonction interlocutoire serait susceptible de
préjudicier irrémédiablement aux droits du requérant. Elle vise à éviter un mal
évident, imminent et irréparable. En cas de doute, la requête devra être
refusée.

Par ailleurs, l'urgence peut résulter non
seulement de faits connus qui laissent croire à l'imminence d'un geste, mais
également du fait qu'un geste appréhendé puisse être posé de façon imprévisible
et qu'une fois posé, on ne puisse y remédier. Cependant, il ne suffit pas
d'alléguer simplement qu'un préjudice aléatoire est susceptible de survenir.

(References omitted)

[
37
]

The Plaintiffs invite the Court to conclude that
an emergency situation exists because of the likelihood that Feldman is on a
mission to seek information on them and to publish, through the media or
through documentaries or otherwise, material which will be defamatory and prejudicial
to their basic human rights. They argue that urgency can build and that the
passing of time adds to it
[13]
.

[
38
]

The Court does not agree that a situation of urgency
exists which allows it to issue the injunction at the provisional stage.

[
39
]

As early as September 2019, the Plaintiffs knew
that Feldman was stating to several people that Lande had misappropriated the
estate of Delphiner and that “if he (Feldman) went down, he would bring Irwin
down with him”

[
40
]

As early as March 31, 2020, in the Affidavit,
Feldman writes that none of the properties which Lande is involved in belong to
him but that they belong to the survivors of the Holocaust or the associations
which represent these survivors. He claims that “it will be my efforts … to put
an immediate halt to his (Lande’s) ongoing crime”.

[
41
]

In one video he shot
[14]
, which the Court is unable to
date but which was filed with the Amended Application, Feldman introduces
himself as a lawyer and real estate developer from Montreal, Canada, who has
discovered that his partner has been living off Nazi looted gold valued at 3.2 $
billion and announces that he is on a relentless mission to get to the bottom
of this and give the money back to whom it belongs.

[
42
]

In another video
[15]
, shot sometime in April 2020
and also filed with the Amended Application, Feldman accuses his partner, whom
he does not name, to live off the “forbidden fruit” of gold stolen by the Nazis
and states that the only thing worse than that is to watch him live off the
forbidden fruit.

[
43
]

In other words, many allegations of both the
Application and the Amended Application state in detail Feldman’s actions which
purport either to defame the Plaintiffs or put their privacy or security at
risk. The allegations were serious enough that complaints were made to the
police and Feldman arrested.

[
44
]

The Article brings the conflict between the
parties up to another level in that, based on the evidence available to the
Court, Feldman is the one who created the opportunity for the Article to be
published and the mere publishing of the Article brings Feldman’s allegations
toward Lande in the public eye.

[
45
]

Is it likely that the average reader of the
Article will retain that it is generally based on extracts from judicial
proceedings? Is it likely that Lande’s reputation and his wife’s have been hurt
by the Article? Without having to answer these questions, the Court feels that
the Article does not create, even when added to the other facts alleged to have
occurred since September of 2019, a situation where an urgency is created by
the likelihood of an unforeseeable illegal act to be posed by Feldman.

[
46
]

In the Court’s view, the Article does not create
a situation of urgency which allows it to issue a provisional interlocutory
injunction.

[
47
]

The Court understands the Plaintiffs’
exasperation, notably with the fact that the ongoing saga between the parties
has been brought into the public eye. However, with respect for the contrary
view, it is of the opinion that the situation does not create an urgency which
warrants that the Court issue, without evidence being adduced, orders such as
the ones they seek.

FOR THESE
REASONS, THE COURT:

[
48
]

DISMISSES
the Motion
for the Issuance of a Provisional Injunction;

[
49
]

With costs.
